newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says 30 Kurdish rebels killed in clashes.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says 30 Kurdish rebels killed in clashes.

text.p: Turkish troops supported by air power have killed 30 Kurdish rebels in clashes in southeastern Turkey, state-run Anatolian news agency said on Monday.
It quoted the emergency rule governor's office as saying the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas died in fighting over the previous 24 hours in the mountainous Sirnak province.
One Turkish soldier died in the clashes, it said.
According to military sources, around 160 PKK rebels were killed in the last week during a cross-border operation by Turkish troops into northern Iraq.
They said Turkish F-4 fighter-bombers continued to bomb PKK camps in the region over the weekend. Iraq has condemned Turkey for pursuing the rebels into Iraqi territory.
The PKK uses bases in northern Iraq outside Baghdad's control as part of its guerrilla war for self-rule in southeast Turkey. Turkish troops have crossed into Iraq several times in large numbers.
More than 21,000 people have been killed in the 12-year-old conflict.
